solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurt fly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sting or ache
second meaning: sharp and streetwise, as in 'a fly operator'

explanation.surface: Someone has injured an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as the insect, but here it is the informal adjective for knowing and quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for feeling a stinging pain and as an adjective for clever or sharp-witted.

clue.text: South African dog struggling during run, one's not eating healthily?

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the jumbled letters sit inside the run
something struggling is thrashing about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights

explanation.surface: A South African dog, struggling on a run, is clearly on a poor diet.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in tights. 'Salad dodger' is jocular British slang for an overweight person.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad dodger is a humorous term for someone who avoids healthy food and is overweight.

clue.text: Space around Saturn's farthest ring

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the space goes round the letter
the farthest part of a word is its very last letter

explanation.surface: An astronomy note about the outermost ring of Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like part of the planet's description, but it is the definition, as in a boxing or circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area for sport or shows, just as a circus or boxing ring is.

clue.text: Ringing of bells in Brussels, unbearably loudly, always starts in Hergé's Belgium?

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the following phrase

parts.note: Hergé created Tintin, a Belgian boy reporter, so Belgium is jokingly Tintin nation

indicators.note: starts means the first letter of each of these words

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Church bells clang deafeningly across Brussels, home of the cartoonist Hergé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' is both a link and the last of the initial-letter words; the question mark flags the jokey Tintin nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintinnabulation is the ringing or jingling sound of bells, from Latin tintinnabulum, a little bell.

clue.text: Gripping device getting kid across slope

indicators.note: to get a thing across something is to stretch it from one side to the other, so it surrounds

parts.note: to kid is to fool or con

explanation.surface: A climber's tool lets a youngster get over an incline.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is the spiked plate a climber fixes to a boot to grip ice.

clue.text: A way to break up black fuel that's along the shore

indicators.note: breaking something up means splitting it apart, so the other part goes into the gap

parts.note: A, then ST for street, a way

explanation.surface: A method to smash up lumps of coal by the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal describes what lies along the coast, so beside or along the shore of the sea.

clue.text: Starters having an edge over drink

indicators.note: in a down answer over places the earlier part above the drink

parts.note: a tip is an edge or point
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Appetisers that beat a drink, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having an edge over' reads as being slightly better than, but it builds the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, the starters of the menu.

clue.text: Spoilt on poodles, big ruby

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so these letters are wrecked and reformed

explanation.surface: Pampered on poodles, a big red jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon's blood is the deep red shade of the finest rubies, used as a colour name for it.

clue.text: Never receiving pass, records dropping off unexpectedly?

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the other words go inside

parts.note: nary is dialect for not one, never a
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A sports fan never gets a pass to the records, and nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' looks like falling, but it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcolepsy is a disorder causing sudden, uncontrollable bouts of sleep, so nodding off without warning.

clue.text: Run well within a corporation, there's high growth

indicators.note: within means inside, so these words sit inside the corporation

parts.note: A, then TUM, since corporation is old slang for a paunch or stomach
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a bore is a narrow well drilled for water

explanation.surface: Business advice: keep the cash flowing inside a big company and it will grow fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company, but it is a dated jokey word for a pot belly, here TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden of trees, a place where there is tall growth.

clue.text: A politician contracted to share the same view

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: An MP signed a deal to back the same opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like signing a contract, but it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree with someone is to be of one mind, holding the same opinion as them.

clue.text: Serious setback, as line by party taken the wrong way when in front

indicators.note: when placed in, so the reversed letters sit inside the front

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

indicators.note: the wrong way means backwards, so these letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: A political party misreads its line and loses badly at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like a political front, but it is a ship's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is a punch to the torso, and figuratively a severe setback or disappointment.

clue.text: Quit securing entrance to garden with gum

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the gum wraps round the letter

parts.note: resin is a gum from trees

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stopped sealing the garden gate with glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a job or position, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Reference the end for so many old beasts?

parts.words: end for so many old beasts
parts.note: dinosaur names like brontosaurus and stegosaurus end this way

explanation.surface: A source explaining how the dinosaurs died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' suggests extinction, but it is the ending of the names of prehistoric beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words grouped by meaning, with synonyms.

clue.text: Balloonist's long time for flying about

indicators.note: flying about means flitting here and there, so these letters scatter

explanation.surface: An aviator has waited ages to go up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Montgolfier brothers launched the first manned hot-air balloon flight, in France in 1783.

clue.text: Initial wage extremely terrible, prepare to attack

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so these letters come out in a different order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the two ends of the word

explanation.surface: A worker's starting pay is dreadful, so they get ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to stay hidden ready to ambush, which is preparing to attack.

clue.text: Ultimately unedifying, entire novel written about most indecent author

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word
written about means set down around something, enclosing it
novel means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A whole uninspiring novel by an obscene writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split in two so that they can wrap round the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was an American modernist writer, so she is an example of an author.

clue.text: Recorder returning passport, noble for the most part

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a passport is a form of ID

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An official taking back the travel document of an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist records each day's events in a journal, so is a recorder.

clue.text: Request for model

explanation.surface: Asking someone to sit as an artist's model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but it gives PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward a suggestion or offer, close to making a request.

clue.text: Moment one monster and knight devoured by witch

parts.note: monster as an adjective means huge

indicators.note: what is devoured ends up inside the eater

parts.note: an old bag is an unpleasant old woman, like a witch
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale moment where a monster and a knight are eaten by a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moment one' means the very first moment of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the event that began the universe, the first instant of time itself.

clue.text: Order designed, he'll go with posh, long coat on him?

indicators.note: an instruction to put the following letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor is told that a smart gent will wear a specially designed long coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the long coat is the dog's shaggy fur, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old English Sheepdog is a breed known for its very long, thick shaggy coat.

clue.text: Comatose affair, head of maths gatecrashing rave

parts.note: a do is an affair or party

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes in uninvited, so the letter goes inside
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A maths teacher crashes a dance party and ends up out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' looks like the dance party, but it is the verb to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, which is close to comatose in its sense of unresponsive.

clue.text: Freedom of movement allowed a little drama

parts.note: play is room to move, as in a rope with some play

explanation.surface: Being allowed to move freely caused a minor fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little drama' looks like a fuss, but it means a short play.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlet is a short stage play, so a small dramatic piece.

clue.text: Head scratched in principled test

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, and scratching it removes it

explanation.surface: Something about a head being scratched during an ethical examination.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, such as a language exam, so it is a kind of test.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen rent shop

parts.note: conveniences are public toilets, marked Ladies and Gentlemen
rent as the past tense of rend, tore

explanation.surface: An announcement to an audience about leasing a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public convenience is a public toilet, signed Ladies and Gentlemen. 'rent' looks like hire, but it is the past of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A convenience store is a small local shop selling groceries and everyday goods, open long hours.

clue.text: Soldier scoffing a coarse biscuit

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so the food ends up inside

parts.note: A, then RIBALD for coarse or crude

explanation.surface: A soldier wolfing down a hard ration biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with a layer of currants pressed between thin pastry.

clue.text: Voter wiping brow, one reads

indicators.note: the brow is the top of the face, so the word's top letter is wiped away

explanation.surface: A hot, anxious voter mopping their forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lector is a person who reads lessons aloud in church, so one who reads.

clue.text: A mark on liner's bow for a sailor

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: A, then SCAR for a mark

explanation.surface: A scratch on the front of a cruise ship, blamed on a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the mark after the first letter in the across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia, historically crewing European ships.

clue.text: A pretentious type recalled current Japanese art

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: A, then SNOB for a pretentious person
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A snooty person remembered something about modern Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese craft of growing miniature trees in pots, a traditional art form.

clue.text: Kicking entertainment in prison toilet

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
the can is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Prisoners put on a show in the jail lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking French dance from the Moulin Rouge, an entertainment full of kicks.

clue.text: Legitimate place for further distribution

explanation.surface: A proper venue for handing things out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Reallocation is sharing out resources a second time, a further distribution of them.

clue.text: Ground where queen buried in school

indicators.note: what is buried is put inside something else

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The site where a monarch was laid to rest on school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to train.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered for its physical features, so a stretch of ground.

clue.text: Save dollar touring Central American nation

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so these letters move about

explanation.surface: Travel advice: keep your money when visiting a country in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, El Salvador uses the US dollar as its currency.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is the smallest country on the Central American isthmus, bordering the Pacific.

clue.text: Drop career after a month

indicators.note: after places the career below the month in this down answer

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
one's line is one's job or career

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job a month on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a verb meaning to hurtle, but it is the noun for a line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is a fall or decrease, and so is a drop, both as nouns and verbs.

clue.text: Chance taken to confiscate a weapon, she makes statement

indicators.note: to confiscate is to seize and hold, so the bet takes the rest inside

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A woman takes a gamble seizing a weapon, and gives a statement to police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statement' looks like a police statement, but it is a financial one.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance sheet is a financial statement listing a company's assets and liabilities at a date.

clue.text: Darling, it figures, these are fancy

explanation.surface: A sweetheart notes that something makes sense and is elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: A fancy is also a small iced cake, which is what these are.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits fours are tiny decorated cakes served after a meal, classed as fancies in baking.

clue.text: Amateur cutting wild snowdrop for a joke

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it, so the amateur sits inside
wild means unruly, so these letters run in a new order

explanation.surface: An amateur gardener cuts a wild snowdrop for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A play on words is a pun, a joke built on a double meaning or similar sound.

clue.text: Innocent chap thrown in the van

indicators.note: thrown means hurled about, so these letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A blameless man is hurled into the back of a police van.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantechnicon is a large British furniture-removal lorry, a type of big van.

clue.text: Black dresses a shade suggestive ultimately, and forward

indicators.note: dressing something is wrapping it in clothes, so the other parts go inside
ultimately points to the last letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Racy black dresses, in a colour that's suggestive and forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the number eight is a forward who packs down at the back of the scrum. 'forward' looks like brazen, matching the dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: The number eight is a rugby union forward position, the player at the rear of the scrum.

clue.text: Reliable partner among eccentric wet blankets

indicators.note: a blanket covers something, so the wet word wraps round
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A faithful spouse surrounded by odd killjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' looks like a link word, and 'wet blankets' like killjoys, but both split up.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogamist keeps only one partner, so is a faithful and reliable one.

clue.text: A report catching Labour's leader out

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the report goes round it

parts.note: A, then BOOM for the report of a gun

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A news item reveals that the head of the Labour Party has been forced out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the end of the political story, but it describes flowers that are out, in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that are out have opened their flowers, so they are blooming.

clue.text: Civic dignitary or duke, male punching sovereign after uprising

indicators.note: a punch goes into its target, so these letters go inside
an uprising goes up, and in a down answer that means the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A rebellion sees a duke or male noble attacking the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lord Mayor is the ceremonial head of a major British city, a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Retiring, an artist in Japanese city

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the short word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A shy painter is living in a city in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagoya is a major industrial port city on Honshu, one of Japan's largest.

clue.text: Flanked by a couple of maidens, king is after queen — a habit

indicators.note: to be flanked is to have something on each side, so the rest sits between them

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; two of them

indicators.note: after places the king and is behind the queen in the order

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of England
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal court tableau: a king follows his queen between two young ladies-in-waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannerism is a distinctive personal gesture or way of speaking that someone repeats habitually.

clue.text: Forty or fifty died on the field — something irritating thing about it?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the insect wraps round the other parts

parts.note: a midge is a tiny biting fly
D for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone in their forties dies out in the fields, killed by some pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog copy of this clue has a stray word: 'something' and 'thing' overlap, and either can go with 'irritating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle age is the period of life roughly from forty to sixty, so ages like forty or fifty.

clue.text: A hundred having alighted from coach on river, refreshments served here

indicators.note: to alight is to get off, so the letter gets out of the word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A hundred passengers get off a coach by a river, where a café awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a bus, but it is the verb to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A teahouse is a café where tea and light refreshments are served.

clue.text: Fine dish not required with vegetable soup ingredient

indicators.note: what is not required is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A good meal needs no extra vegetable for the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vegetable' looks like part of the definition, but it is the word that loses its last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods thicken soups and stews such as gumbo, so they are a common soup ingredient.

clue.text: Check certain to control strained setter

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it in check, so these words surround it

parts.note: to rein in is to check

explanation.surface: An instruction to make sure a tense crossword compiler is kept in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but here it means something that sets hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforced concrete is building material with steel bars inside that sets solid, so it is a thing that sets.

clue.text: Far-reaching organisation can tempt others at first into work

indicators.note: into places those letters inside the work
at first points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A huge firm can lure other people into jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: An octopus is used figuratively for an organisation whose influence reaches everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the eight-armed sea creature, a sprawling organisation with tentacles everywhere is called an octopus.

clue.text: Disagreement during meal

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A spat at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' looks like a container signal, but it gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch or midday meal.

clue.text: Weak devil consumed by desire

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed, so it ends up inside the other word

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A feeble demon eaten up by longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimpish means feeble and lacking courage, like a wimp, so it is a synonym of weak.

clue.text: State squeezing Louisiana, America, on part of a document?

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to grip it tightly between, so it goes inside

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: California pressing on Louisiana and the rest of America over a document.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals an unusual definition: 'on' means relating to.
explanation.definitionFit: Clausal means relating to a clause, and a clause is a section of a legal document.

clue.text: Comfortable, copper retiring

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A modest policeman is at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like a reversal signal, but here it means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job or life is easy and comfortable, needing little effort.

clue.text: Willing to investigate cause of mischief?

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Keen to find out what caused some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' seems to mean eager, but it means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone testate has left a valid legal will at death, so in a punning sense was willing.

clue.text: Animated answer, as it happens

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: A lively reply given on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean lively, full of energy and spirit, which is one sense of animated.

clue.text: Remarkably funny horse is a joy to be with

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually amusing horse is great company.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of sunshine is a cheerful person who brightens others' day, someone delightful company.

clue.text: Favourable feature of phone: roaming

parts.note: an app is a program on a smartphone

explanation.surface: A good review of the roaming function on a mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Approving means showing approval, so a favourable reaction or opinion of something.

clue.text: Farm building enclosing field and lake in a peculiar way

indicators.note: to enclose is to surround, so the rest goes inside the building

parts.note: a sty is a pig pen
a range is open grazing land
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A pigsty walling in a meadow and a pond, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely is the adverb from strange, meaning oddly or peculiarly.

clue.text: More than one adder proceeds uncertainly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who tot up figures

explanation.surface: Several snakes slither along shakily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adder' looks like the snake, but it is someone who adds, a totter.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means people who tot up sums, and the verb means walks with an unsteady, wobbling gait.

clue.text: Finally, code opening case

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: At last the secret code to open the briefcase.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, and a case is an instance of something happening, as in 'in that event'.
